topics.name: No sooner ... than / Hardly ... when / As soon as
Too ... to / so ... that / such ... that
Past and perfect tenses in a story

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Yesterday the poet wrote some funny lines.
Yesterday the poet writes some funny lines.
Yesterday the poet has written some funny lines.
questions.rule: Yesterday is a finished past time, so use the simple past wrote, not the present perfect.

options: The lines were too funny that I laughed loudly.
The lines were so funny that I laughed loudly.
The lines were so funny than I laughed loudly.
questions.rule: The pattern is so + adjective + that. 'Too' goes with 'to', and 'than' is for comparisons.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last night shows the past, so use the simple past: laughed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use too + adjective + to to say something could not be done: too tired to walk.

questions.before: No sooner had he read the first line
questions.rule: No sooner always pairs with than.
Use What before a noun phrase (funny lines). How goes before an adjective alone: How funny they were!
Exclamation pattern: How + adjective + subject + verb!

chat: Did you finish the funny poem last night?
options: Yes, I did. I finished it at ten o'clock.
Yes, I was. I finished it at ten o'clock.
Yes, I done. I finish it at ten o'clock.
questions.rule: A Did ...? question takes the short answer Yes, I did, and the past needs finished.

questions.source: What a loud roar the servant gave!
options: The servant gave very a loud roar.
The servant gives a very loud roar.
The servant gave a very loud roar.
questions.rule: What a ...! becomes a statement with a very ...; keep the past tense gave.

questions.source: The joke was too silly to print.
options: The joke was so silly that it could not be printed.
The joke was so silly that it could not printed.
The joke was very silly that it could not be printed.
questions.rule: too ... to becomes so ... that ... not; 'was' is past, so use could not.

options: Hardly he had read the line when he grinned.
Hardly had he read the line when he grinned.
Hardly had he read the line than he grinned.
questions.rule: Hardly takes inversion (had he) and pairs with when, not 'than'.

options: How a funny poem it is!
What a funny poem it is!
questions.rule: With a singular noun use What a + adjective + noun!

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: No sooner is always followed by than, never 'when'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Holmes is one person and 'that day' is past, so use was.
so + adverb + that shows the result: so hard that buttons burst.

questions.after: the poem, I watched his face.
questions.rule: An action going on in the past when another happened takes the past continuous: was reading.
No sooner + had + subject + past participle ... than + simple past.

chat: Why didn't you read your poem aloud?
options: It was too funny that I can't read it.
It was too funny for me to read without laughing.
It was so funny to read without laughing.
questions.rule: too + adjective + for me + to-verb is correct. 'Too' never goes with 'that'.

chat: When did the class start laughing?
options: As soon as Rohan read the first line, everyone laughed.
As soon as Rohan had read the first line, everyone laughs.
No sooner Rohan read the first line than everyone laughed.
questions.rule: As soon as + simple past, then simple past. 'No sooner' needs inversion: No sooner had Rohan read.

questions.source: As soon as the servant read the fourth line, he broke into a roar.
options: No sooner the servant read the fourth line than he broke into a roar.
No sooner had the servant read the fourth line when he broke into a roar.
No sooner had the servant read the fourth line than he broke into a roar.
questions.rule: No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than ...

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: By the time the doctor came, the servant had laughed for an hour.
By the time the doctor came, the servant has laughed for an hour.
By the time the doctor had come, the servant laughs for an hour.
questions.rule: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: had laughed before the doctor came.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had already posted.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After to use the base form of the verb: able to keep.

questions.before: Hardly had the poem reached the press
questions.rule: Hardly pairs with when; No sooner pairs with than.

questions.after: funny for anyone to read with a straight face.
questions.rule: too + adjective + for someone + to-verb means it could not be done.
too + adjective + to + verb: too weak to stand.

chat: What were you doing when the lights went out?
options: I was reading a funny poem to my grandmother.
I am reading a funny poem to my grandmother.
I was read a funny poem to my grandmother.
questions.rule: What were you doing ...? asks about an action in progress in the past: I was reading.

chat: My uncle laughed so much that his shirt button flew off!
options: What funny sight that must have been!
What a funny sight that must have been!
How a funny sight that must have been!
questions.rule: A singular noun after What needs a: What a funny sight!

questions.source: The servant read the sixth line. Then he tumbled in a fit.
options: After the servant has read the sixth line, he tumbled in a fit.
After the servant had read the sixth line, he tumbled in a fit.
After the servant had read the sixth line, he tumbles in a fit.
questions.rule: The first action takes the past perfect had read; the later one stays simple past tumbled.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Yesterday needs wrote; No sooner pairs with than; the result is past too: fell.

options: The lines were so funny that neither of us could stopped laughing.
The lines were such funny that neither of us could stop laughing.
The lines were so funny that neither of us could stop laughing.
questions.rule: so + adjective + that; after could use the base verb stop. 'Such' needs a noun.

options: The poem was send to the printer last week.
The poem has been sent to the printer last week.
The poem was sent to the printer last week.
questions.rule: Last week needs the simple past; the passive is was + past participle (sent).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Mr Bose is one person and last night is past, so use was laughing.

questions.after: not written a funny line since that day.
questions.rule: Since + a point in time takes the present perfect; 'the poet' is singular, so has.
What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb! After 'by' use the -ing form: by sending.

chat: Did you catch the school bus on time?
options: No. Hardly had I reached the stop when the bus left.
No. Hardly I had reached the stop when the bus left.
No. Hardly had I reach the stop when the bus left.
questions.rule: Hardly had + subject + past participle ... when: Hardly had I reached.

chat: Can you lift this box of books for me?
options: Sorry, it's so heavy for me to lift.
Sorry, it's too heavy that I can lift.
Sorry, it's too heavy for me to lift.
questions.rule: too heavy for me to lift = I cannot lift it. 'So' needs 'that', and 'too' needs 'to'.

questions.source: The man was so weak that he could not get out of bed.
options: The man was too weak to get out of bed.
The man was too weak to got out of bed.
The man was too weak that he could get out of bed.
questions.rule: so ... that ... could not becomes too ... to; 'too' already carries the 'not'.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Raju (he) loves; Last Sunday needs told; Hardly pairs with when.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: The story is past, so could not; the past of send is sent, not 'sended'.

options: Scarcely the servant had read the fifth line when his waistband split.
Scarcely had the servant read the fifth line than his waistband split.
Scarcely had the servant read the fifth line when his waistband split.
questions.rule: Scarcely, like hardly, needs inversion (had the servant read) and pairs with when.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The main clause is past perfect continuous, so the time clause takes the simple past: arrived.

questions.after: a silly joke that even the serious printer laughed.
questions.rule: Before a + adjective + noun use such: such a silly joke that ...
Hardly + had + subject + past participle ... when + simple past.

chat: Did the guests enjoy your funny speech?
options: Yes! No sooner I had begun than they started clapping.
Yes! No sooner had I begun than they started clapping.
Yes! No sooner had I began than they started clapping.
questions.rule: No sooner had I + past participle: the participle of begin is begun, not 'began'.

questions.source: The servant was a very mighty man.
options: What mighty man the servant was!
What a mighty man the servant was!
How a mighty man the servant was!
questions.rule: a very + adjective + noun becomes What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb!

questions.source: As soon as the poet saw the servant's face, he regretted the joke.
options: Hardly had the poet seen the servant's face when he regretted the joke.
Hardly had the poet saw the servant's face when he regretted the joke.
Hardly the poet had seen the servant's face when he regretted the joke.
questions.rule: Hardly had + subject + past participle (seen) ... when ...

questions.source: The servant had read all six lines.
options: All six lines have been read by the servant.
All six lines had read by the servant.
All six lines had been read by the servant.
questions.rule: Past perfect passive = had been + past participle.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Tara (she) was; plural tears were; No sooner pairs with than.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: so ... that, not 'too ... that'; the story is past, so laughed and knocked.
